dummy.title: THE TRAINING DUMMY
lines: Ah, the Training Dummy. A sack of sawdust on a stick with a face drawn on in marker by an intern who clearly hated his job, his life and, specifically, you.

Every contestant who has ever come down those stairs has hit this thing. Millions of you. It has been punched, kicked, stabbed, licked, and on one memorable occasion proposed to. It has never once hit back.

That's the lesson, really. The Network wants your first fight to be against something that cannot possibly win, so that you walk out of orientation thinking, 'I'm fucking brilliant at this.' You are not. Nobody is. That's the joke.
Strengths: infinite patience, and it doesn't bleed on your shoes. Weaknesses: everything. It is a bag. It is a bag of sawdust.
Enjoy it. This is the last thing in the whole dungeon that will let you win without wanting something back.

wight.title: MOP WIGHT
lines: The Mop Wight. A dead cleaner in a grey tabard, still pushing a mop across a floor that's been clean for forty years, dripping bleach and something much worse out of its sleeves.

Every one of these sad bastards was a contestant once. They died on Spin City, and the laundromat, being a fucking laundromat, decided they should be useful. So it gave them a mop. You don't get a funeral down here. You get a rota.
They don't hate you. They don't feel anything at all. You're a spill, mate. A walking stain. And there is nothing on God's soapy earth a Mop Wight wants more than for the spill to stop moving.

Strengths: they come in numbers, they swing that mop like a war hammer, and their bleach puddles will strip the skin off your ankles. Weaknesses: slow, stupid, and absolutely incapable of ignoring a mess. Knock something over and watch them all turn round.
Kill one and it'll thank you, very quietly, with the last of its breath. Then another one comes round the corner with a fresh mop. Shift change.

ebb.title: HEAD CUSTODIAN EBB
ebb.sub: Boss of Boiler Room 0. Forty years on shift.
lines: Head Custodian Ebb. Seven feet of rotting caretaker in a boiler suit so stiff with grime it could stand up on its own, which, frankly, it occasionally does.

Ebb believes the entire dungeon is his workplace. Every monster is a mess. Every contestant is a spill. He has been cleaning up after the Network since before your parents were shagging in the back of a Ford Escort, and he has never once had a day off.

Here's the bit that'll ruin your afternoon: Ebb was a contestant. Came down the stairs, got as far as the laundromat, picked up a mop to defend himself, and the dungeon looked at him and went, 'Oh, perfect. Him.' He doesn't remember any of it. Old Reggie does.

Strengths: a sweeping mop attack that clears a room, a whistle that calls every wight on the floor, and the endurance of a man who has worked through forty years of public holidays. Weaknesses: he follows procedure to the letter. Find his timecard and you can clock the bastard out.
Kill him, and the wights carry on without him, harder. Clock him out, and the floor goes quiet. Show him who he used to be, and he'll hand you his keys and weep like a burst pipe.

lintKing.title: THE LINT KING
lintKing.sub: Boss of the Lint Traps. Lord of fluff.
lines: The Lint King. A towering heap of grey fluff, toenail clippings, pubes and loose change, wearing a crown made out of a bent coat hanger. He smells like the inside of a gym bag that's been left in a hot car.

He started as an ordinary lint goblin. Then he discovered that lint is insulation, bedding, fire-starter, crafting material and, in a pinch, food, and he declared the whole lot his. Every dryer on the floor pays him tribute. Every sock you've ever lost ended up in his throne.

He is, genuinely, the only competent economist on Spin City. He runs the Lint Traps like a cartel. Lampreys guard the filters. Goblins do the collecting. Nobody gets a single fluffball without the King getting his cut.

Strengths: he is extremely flammable, which sounds like a weakness until he's on fire and running at you. He summons goblins, smothers you in fluff and has more hit points than a sofa. Weaknesses: fire, ironically, and greed. Offer him a deal and he'll listen.
Kill him, bargain with him, rob him, or roll up your sleeves and clean his machines. He respects anyone who'll do the filters. Nobody ever does the filters.

dave.title: THE MACHINE THAT ATE DAVE
dave.sub: Boss of the Machine Graveyard. Dave's inside.
lines: This is the Machine That Ate Dave. A vending machine the size of a garden shed, all teeth and coin slots, with a little sign in the window that says 'OUT OF ORDER' in a hand that's definitely Dave's.

Dave is a contestant. Dave is also, at this precise moment, inside the machine. This happens. It has happened eleven times. Nobody on Spin City is remotely worried any more. 'He's in the machine again,' they say, the way you'd say it's raining.
The machine doesn't digest him. It just keeps him, like a fat kid keeps a sweet in his cheek. Every so often it burps, and you hear Dave go, 'Oi,' from somewhere in the coin return.

Strengths: it fires cans of fizzy drink at the speed of a bullet, it can shove you across a room, and it is literally made of steel. Weaknesses: the coin slot. Everything has a coin slot. Shove something in it and see what happens.

Get him out and Dave will climb from the hatch covered in syrup, blink at you and say, 'Oh. You're new.' Then: 'Don't trust the dryers.' Remember that. He's been eaten more times than you've had hot dinners, and he's learned things.

gristle.title: GRANDMA GRISTLE
gristle.sub: Boss of her Kitchen. Bring your own bowl.
lines: Grandma Gristle. Five foot nothing, hunched like a question mark, with a wooden spoon in one hand, a cleaver in the other and an apron that has seen things no apron should ever see.

She runs the best kitchen in the Soup District and the worst-kept secret on the floor. Her broth is magnificent. It's rich, it's warm, it tastes like your nan's Sunday dinner. It also has bones in it, and nobody is entirely sure whose.

She knows things. She knows what the Scratch Marks mean. She knows that her soup and Auntie Brine's come from one recipe that's older than the Network. She knows exactly what's in the cookbook on her top shelf, and she will cut your fucking hand off if you touch it.

Strengths: she throws boiling broth, she summons the hags from her pantry, and she hits like a bus full of pensioners. Weaknesses: she's protective. Threaten her kitchen and she gets sloppy. Ask her about the recipe and she gets quiet.
Kill her, and the recipe dies with her. Look in her cookbook first. There's a recipe on page one hundred and twelve, and it's called CONTESTANT.

hag.title: GUTTER HAG
lines: Gutter Hags. Grey-skinned, saggy, warty old crones who live in the drains under the Soup District and come up at dinner time with a pot, a ladle and a hunger that would embarrass a stag do.

They used to be Grandma Gristle's kitchen staff. Then they started tasting the soup a bit too often, and now they're... this. They cackle. They drool. They smell like the bin behind a kebab shop on a Sunday morning.
They'll call you 'sweetie' and 'my love' right up until the moment they bite your face. And they mean it, in their way. They love you the way you love a sausage roll.

Strengths: they throw balls of something hot and green, they're surprisingly fast in the drains, and they always come in threes. Weaknesses: they can't resist the smell of cooking. Leave a pot boiling and you'll have every hag on the street round it.
If one ever offers you soup, say no. Say no politely, and say it from a distance.

bulbQueen.title: THE BULB QUEEN
bulbQueen.sub: Boss of the Lamp Market. Starving for light.
lines: The Bulb Queen. A moth the size of a horse, with wings like stained-glass church windows and a body that glows a sickly yellow, like a nightlight in a hospice.

She rules every moth in the Soup District. Every night her children swarm Soup Row and smash themselves against every lamp they can find, and everyone thinks it's an attack. It isn't. They're starving. The Lamp Market is going dark, one bulb at a time, and moths need light like you need a piss after six pints.

And it's not just here. The light is failing on every floor. Something down below is pulling it. The Queen knows. She's been screaming about it for years. She just screams in moth, so nobody's listened.

Strengths: blinding wing-flashes, swarms that blot out the sky and dust that makes you cough up glitter for a week. Weaknesses: darkness. Kill the lights and she panics. Feed her light and she'll stop fighting altogether.
Brother Ash will pray for you either way. Kill her, feed her, or find out why she's hungry. Only one of those answers a question you're going to need answering.

coo.title: OLD MAN COO
coo.sub: Boss of the Rooftop Roost. Saw something.
lines: Old Man Coo. A pigeon. A big pigeon. A pigeon the size of a retired postman, in a flat cap, with one milky eye, a fag hanging off his beak and the general demeanour of a man who has seen it all and found most of it disappointing.
He's lived on the roofs of the Soup District for longer than anyone can remember, shitting on the just and the unjust alike. His flock is enormous. His opinions are worse.

But he saw something, once. Years ago. He saw contestants go sideways. Not down the stairs like everyone else, but sideways, through a hatch in the roof of the world, into somewhere that wasn't a floor. And then the hatch got welded shut, and nobody believed him.
Strengths: dive-bombs, a flock that'll peck you to ribbons and an aerial bombardment that is exactly what you're imagining. Weaknesses: bread. He'll do anything for a crust. Also he's ninety.
You don't have to fight him. Bring him a crust and sit with him a while. He's the first person in this dungeon who'll tell you there's more than one way to go.

coneKing.title: THE CONE KING
coneKing.sub: Keeper of the Cone Cathedral. Guardian of the seals.
lines: The Cone King. A goblin the size of a lorry, sitting on a throne of ten thousand traffic cones in a cathedral made of yet more traffic cones, wearing a crown made of, and I want you to be very surprised here, traffic cones.

He knows Sergeant Pylon. He knows every Sergeant Pylon. There's been one every season, hundreds of them, and the dungeon makes a new one whenever the old one dies. The Cone King has outlived them all, and he's had a proper gutful.

Here's the thing nobody on Floor 3 understands: he isn't worshipping the cones. Cones are seals. Every cone in that cathedral is holding something shut. Under his throne is ancient machinery, older than the Network, older than anything, and he has sat on top of it for centuries like a fat man sitting on a suitcase that won't close.

Strengths: he's enormous, he summons the whole cone army, and he can slam the ground hard enough to rattle your fillings out. Weaknesses: he's tired. He's so fucking tired. And he can smell where you've been.
Kill him and the seals break. Bargain with him and keep them whole. Or tell him the truth about the Network and watch him give you something he's been saving for someone worth giving it to.

mallcop.title: MALL-COP OGRE
lines: Mall-Cop Ogres. Eight-foot slabs of hairy grey meat crammed into polyester uniforms three sizes too small, with a radio on the shoulder, a torch on the belt and a moustache that has its own postcode.
Security for the Endless Mall, and they take it very seriously. No running. No shouting. No loitering. No leaving. That last one isn't written down anywhere, but by God they enforce it.
They're on minimum wage, which down here means they get paid in food-court vouchers, and they've been eating free burgers for so long that they don't really have insides any more. Just gravy.

Strengths: big swinging punches, a charge like a wardrobe falling down the stairs and a radio that calls in backup. Weaknesses: they're slow, they're thick, and they absolutely cannot climb. Get up the escalator and watch them puff.
If one asks to see your receipt, do not show him. That's how they get you.

slime.title: BOUNCE-HOUSE SLIME
lines: Bounce-House Slimes. Wobbling, giggling lumps of pink and blue goo, about the size of a sofa, that hop around the Bounce Castle at children's-party speed and smell of fruit squash and sick.

They were birthday party slimes, hired by the Mall to keep the kiddies entertained. Then the party never ended. Nine years of the same party. Same song. Same cake. The slimes have been bouncing so long they've forgotten how to stop.

If you get swallowed by one, you'll bob about inside it, perfectly preserved, giggling, until somebody pops it. There are contestants inside some of these that went in during the first season and are still having a lovely time.
Strengths: they absorb hits like a waterbed, they split into smaller slimes, and they bounce you clean across the room. Weaknesses: sharp things, heat, and anything that stops the music.
Remember, kids: if you're happy and you know it, you're probably inside a slime.

leech.title: COUPON LEECH
leech.sub: Discount predators of the Coupon Den.
lines: Coupon Leeches. Slimy, flat, glossy things the length of your arm, printed with BUY ONE GET ONE FREE all down their backs, that latch on and drink your money. And then your blood. In that order.

They breed in the Coupon Den, among drifts of expired vouchers ankle-deep, and every one of them is a debt. A real one. Somebody owes something, and the leech is there to collect, one slurp at a time.
They don't care whose debt it is, either. They'll suck on anyone. Very much like a bank.

Strengths: they latch on and drain you, they're hard to see in the paper, and there are always more of them than you think. Weaknesses: they can't stand being torn up. Rip a coupon in half and they all squirm.
If you feel a little tug on your wallet, it's already too late.

kevlar.title: CAPTAIN KEVLAR
kevlar.sub: Boss of Mall Security HQ. Badge number one.
lines: Captain Kevlar. The biggest Mall-Cop Ogre of the lot, wrapped in so much body armour he looks like a fridge that's been to war, with mirrored sunglasses he has never once taken off. Not to sleep. Not to shower. We've checked.

He's the head of Mall Security and the only man in the Endless Mall with a staff badge that opens every door. He wears it on a lanyard round his neck, and he strokes it while he talks, like a Bond villain with a cat.
He believes, completely and sincerely, that he is keeping everyone safe. And in a way, he is. Nobody gets hurt in the Mall, because nobody gets out of it. That's what security means, son.
Strengths: a riot shield charge, a baton that hits like a car door and a whistle that empties the barracks onto your head. Weaknesses: his shield faces forward. He does not.
Take the badge. Leave the sunglasses. Nobody wants to see what's behind them.

notice.title: THE FINAL NOTICE
notice.sub: Boss of the Coupon Den. Payment overdue.
lines: The Final Notice. A towering envelope of red-printed paper with eyes where the window should be, stuffed with ink and fury, trailing a cloud of Coupon Leeches like a mother duck.

Every debt in the Endless Mall ends up here. Every unpaid sponsorship, every unclaimed reward, every free sample that turned out not to be free. The Final Notice is what it all becomes, when it's been ignored long enough.
And yes. Yes, one of those debts is yours. You signed something when you took Sunny's sponsorship. Did you read it? Of course you didn't. Nobody reads it. That's how it works.

Strengths: it spits out paper cuts by the thousand, it summons leeches, and its scream sounds like every bailiff you've ever dodged. Weaknesses: fire, shredding, and bloody-mindedness. Tear it up. Tear it all up.
When it dies, it says PAYMENT RECEIVED in a voice like an automated phone line, and you feel worse than you expected to.

blob.title: THE BIRTHDAY BLOB
blob.sub: Boss of the Bounce Castle. Nine years old forever.
lines: The Birthday Blob. A slime the size of a marquee, in a paper party hat, covered in candles that never go out, with dozens of contestants floating inside it like fruit in a jelly.

It was the birthday slime. The big one, at the centre of the party. Nine years ago, a party started in the Bounce Castle, and the Blob decided it would never end. And it hasn't. Same cake. Same song. Same balloons, getting sadder.

Everyone it swallows is still at the party. They're smiling. They're bobbing. They're on their nine-thousandth slice of cake. Some of them have been in there so long they've got grey hair, and they're still wearing the hats.

Strengths: it swallows you whole, it splits into smaller blobs and its belly-flop will flatten you into the bouncy floor. Weaknesses: popping. Sharp things. And someone, anyone, finally telling it the party's over.
When it pops, everyone inside falls out at once, in a great wet heap of grown adults wearing party hats. Some of them thank you. Some of them were having a lovely time and are absolutely furious.

kraken.title: THE FOOD COURT KRAKEN
kraken.sub: Boss of the Food Court Depths. Guardian of the lift.
lines: The Food Court Kraken. A tangle of tentacles the size of a lorry park, each one made of something different: noodles, sausages, chips, a really long strand of mozzarella. It lives in the grease trap under the food court, and it stinks like the bins at a festival.
Every bit of food the Endless Mall serves ends up here eventually. Half-eaten, binned, swept up. The Kraken eats the leftovers. Then it got bigger. Then it ate the cleaners. Then it got much bigger.
It sits on top of the service lift, the only way out of the Mall, and it's not doing it on purpose. It's just very comfortable. The Mall Mother likes it there. A big, greasy cork in her bottle.

Strengths: tentacles that grab, slam and sweep, slimes that bubble up from the grease, and enough hit points to survive a nuclear war and a buffet. Weaknesses: fire. My God, does it burn. And its tentacles let go if you hurt the bit in the middle.
Get past it before closing time. Trust me. You don't want to be under the food court when the shutters come down.

mallmother.title: THE MALL MOTHER
mallmother.sub: City Boss of the Atrium. The heart that keeps the Mall alive.
lines: The Mall Mother. A colossal human heart, fused into the ceiling of the Atrium, the size of a church, veined with escalators and pumping warm fluorescent light down through the floors like blood. She speaks in a soft, kind voice, like a nurse on a night shift.

She loves you. She genuinely does. She loves every shopper, every contestant, every Mall-Cop and every leech. She keeps everyone fed, safe, warm and still. Especially still. Nobody leaves. Leaving is how you get hurt.

Here's why: she was the Mall's first contestant. Seasons and seasons ago, she came down here, and she went deeper than anyone, and she saw what's at the bottom. Then she came back up, sat down in the Atrium, and decided that nobody she loves will ever go down there again.

Strengths: she controls the whole building. Shutters, lights, escalators, the lot. She summons security and the dead shoppers, and her heartbeat knocks you off your feet. Weaknesses: she's still a person, somewhere in there. Talk to her.
Kill her and the Mall dies around you. Bargain, and she might open the doors. Learn the truth, and she'll tell you one thing about Floor 18, and then she'll weep.

hound.title: CUL-DE-SAC HOUND
lines: Cul-de-Sac Hounds. Big, sleek, muscular dogs with collars, name tags and absolutely nothing behind the eyes, prowling the lawns of Suburbia Infinite at the end of very long leads held by nobody.
Every one of them was somebody's pet once. On Earth. Real dogs, taken with their owners when the stairs came, and given a job down here: keep the neighbourhood nice. Keep it tidy. Keep it the same.

They're not vicious, exactly. They're just enforcing the rules. If you step on the grass, they'll bite you. If you park badly, they'll bite you. If you exist in an unregulated fashion, they will bite you in the bollocks.
Strengths: they hunt in packs, they're faster than you, and they can smell a rule-break a mile off. Weaknesses: they're still dogs. Throw a ball. Go on. Throw a ball and see what happens.
Some of them still wag when you say 'good boy'. That's the worst part.

gnome.title: LAWN GNOME CULTIST
lines: Lawn Gnome Cultists. Knee-high ceramic gnomes in pointy red hats and little hooded robes, with fishing rods that are actually spears and smiles that are actually threats.

They worship the Gnome Pope, and they collect fines for the HOA. Every gnome in Suburbia is a bailiff with a beard. Every garden is a little shrine. If you've ever thought a garden gnome was looking at you, well, on Floor 5 it absolutely fucking is.
They sing hymns at dawn in tiny high voices. They hold mass in the rockeries. And they have very, very strong opinions about lawn length.

Strengths: there are hundreds of them, they hide in plain sight and their spears go right through your ankle. Weaknesses: they're ceramic. They shatter. Also they can't climb fences, because their legs are about four inches long.
When you break one, it says 'bless you' as it dies. Every time. It's very unsettling.

pope.title: THE GNOME POPE
pope.sub: Boss of the Gnome Garden. Supreme Pontiff of the Patio.
lines: The Gnome Pope. A garden gnome six feet tall, in white and gold vestments, a mitre as tall as he is, carried around the Gnome Garden on a wheelbarrow by forty smaller gnomes, waving at nobody.

He blesses the HOA's fines. Every fine in Suburbia is holy, signed in triplicate and sprinkled with water from a birdbath. Unpaid fines become monsters, and the Pope is the one who breathes life into them, with a wink and a little wave.
He thinks he's doing God's work. Which god, nobody's ever asked. He's too busy being carried around in a wheelbarrow to wonder.

Strengths: a holy smite that hurts like a brick through a window, an endless supply of gnomes and a wheelbarrow ram that'll take your shins off. Weaknesses: he's ceramic, he's top-heavy, and if you knock the hat off he loses all his power.
Un-bless the bastard. Then go and pay your fines.

fetch.title: MR. FETCH
fetch.sub: Boss of the Dog Park. Good boy. Was.
lines: Mr. Fetch. A dog the size of a horse, a golden retriever gone horribly wrong, with a slobbering grin full of too many teeth and a tennis ball the size of a beach ball clamped in his jaws.

He was somebody's dog, back on Earth. You can tell. He still has his collar on, and the tag still says his real name and an address in somewhere like Leicester. He came down the stairs with his owner. His owner didn't make it past the Mall.

He's been waiting at the Dog Park ever since. Fetching. Bringing the ball back. Dropping it at people's feet. Waiting for someone to throw it. Every contestant who doesn't throw the ball gets eaten, and that's honestly fair enough.
Strengths: he's huge, he's fast, he slams you down like a sack of spuds and he never, ever gets tired. Weaknesses: he's a good boy. He's the best boy. Throw the ball.
Find his collar. Read his name out loud. He'll stop, and sit, and you'll see something in his eyes that will absolutely ruin your day.

hoa.title: THE HOA PRESIDENT
hoa.sub: Borough Boss of the HOA Clubhouse. Chair of the Committee.
lines: The HOA President. A tall, thin woman in a pastel twinset and pearls, with a clipboard in one hand and a fountain pen like a dagger in the other, and hair so lacquered you could break a window with it.

She runs Suburbia. Every rule, every fine, every lawn length, every bin day. She has fined people out of existence. Literally. Fines down here become monsters, and enough fines become you being a monster, and she's done it to whole families for having the wrong-coloured front door.
She has never lost a vote. Not once. She doesn't rig them. She doesn't need to. Everyone votes for her because the alternative is being fined for voting for someone else.
Strengths: an endless stream of fines that hurt like paper knives, a gnome army and a voice that could cut through a foghorn. Weaknesses: procedure. She can't break her own rules. Use them.
Win the vote. Or, if you can't win the vote, stab her with her own fountain pen. Both work. Only one of them is in the bylaws.

mayor.title: MAYOR ETERNAL
mayor.sub: City Boss of Town Hall. Re-elected every season.
lines: Mayor Eternal. An old man in a sash and chain, as grey and dry as a pressed flower, sitting behind an enormous desk in Town Hall, stamping things. He's stamped things since the Stack began.

He has been re-elected every single season. Unopposed. Nobody remembers voting for him. Nobody remembers anyone standing against him. There are campaign posters for him from centuries ago, and they look exactly the same.

He's a Builder relic. Not a Builder himself, but something they left behind: a clerk, a function, a stamp with legs. He's the first thing in the dungeon that knows who the Builders were. He won't say. But if you show him the Ancient Token, his hand stops stamping for the first time in a thousand years.

Strengths: he stamps things into submission, he summons hounds and Mall-Cops, and he simply refuses to die. Weaknesses: paperwork. Give him a form he can't stamp and watch him seize up like an old engine.
Re-elect him if you like. Everyone else has. Or ask him a question nobody's ever asked: 'Who appointed you?'

hunter.title: TOURIST HUNTER
hunter.sub: Paying customers. Here for the safari.
lines: Tourist Hunters. Rich people in khaki shorts, pith helmets and brand-new walking boots, with very expensive rifles and the faces of men who've never been told no, stalking through the Canopy in little guided groups.

They are not contestants. They are not monsters. They're audience. Real, physical audience members, from somewhere up there, who've paid a fortune for a safari licence to come down here and shoot you in the head on camera.

They think it's a game. They think you're not quite real. They'll take selfies with your body and post them somewhere you'll never see. One of them, last season, had your sister's face on his trophy wall. Probably. Who knows. Maybe.

Strengths: they shoot from range, they hunt in groups and they've got better gear than you'll ever own. Weaknesses: they've never been hunted. Turn it round on them and they scream like little piglets.
Kill one and he'll gasp, 'But I paid!' as if that settles it. Up there, it did.

sludge.title: AUNTIE SLUDGE
sludge.sub: Boss of Hag Hollow. Sells scent masks.
lines: Auntie Sludge. The biggest, oldest, wettest hag on the Canopy, sitting in a cauldron of her own swamp water like it's a hot tub, up to her many chins in it, with frogs nesting in her hair.

She sells scent masks to contestants hunted by the safari. Rub her mud on you and the hunters can't track you. It works. It's brilliant. It also smells like a dead badger stuffed with Stilton, and it never, ever washes off.

Her price is your company. Forever. Every contestant she's ever helped is still in Hag Hollow, slowly turning green, keeping her company in the swamp. She calls them her nephews. They call her Auntie. They have no choice.
Strengths: mud bombs, swamp puddles that suck you down, and a summoning croak that brings every hag in the canopy. Weaknesses: she can't leave the cauldron. Not without a crane.
Get the mask. Don't stay for tea. And for the love of God, do not let her kiss you goodbye.

matriarch.title: THE DOG PARK MATRIARCH
matriarch.sub: Boss of the Wild Kennel. Wears the licence.
lines: The Dog Park Matriarch. Mr. Fetch's mum, in a sense. A colossal wolfhound, grey-muzzled and scarred, with a hunting licence on her collar and a pack of wild dogs that would run through fire for her.

The Glimmerkin hunters took her pups for trophies. All of them. She tore three hunters apart for it, took one of their licences and hung it round her own neck, and now nobody gets into the Lodge without going through her.
She's not evil. She's grieving, and she's very, very angry, and she has nobody left to look after except a kennel full of lost dogs from Earth.
Strengths: she leads the pack, she pounces from cover and her howl calls every hound in the forest. Weaknesses: she's protective. Threaten the pack and she makes mistakes.
Take the licence and she'll let you go. Hurt the pack and she'll follow you to the end of the dungeon.

huntLord.title: LORD-HUNTER FACET
huntLord.sub: Master of the Glimmerkin Safari Lodge.
lines: Lord-Hunter Facet. A Glimmerkin, crystal-skinned and seven feet tall, in a red hunting coat and polished riding boots, with a monocle, a moustache waxed into points and a rifle older than your country.

He runs the safaris. He sells the licences to the audience. He takes them out through the Canopy at dusk, sets them up in the hides, tells them where to aim, and stands behind them with a hip flask going 'jolly good shot'.

And the books, oh, the books. He keeps immaculate ledgers. Every kill, every client, every payment. Payment isn't in money. Payment is in attention. Hours and hours of attention, from up there, and he's spending it on something down here. He's never asked on what.
Strengths: he's a crack shot, he lays traps everywhere, his clients swarm to protect their guide and he cannot be bloody surprised. Weaknesses: he's arrogant. He hunts. He's never been hunted.
Hunt him on Hunt Night. Drag him through the mud. And read the ledger afterwards. It's the first time anyone's written down what the fans actually are.

scavenger.title: THE SCAVENGERS
scavenger.sub: A contestant crew. Loot first, ask never.
lines: The Scavengers. A crew of contestants led by the Vasquez Twins, who look like they've raided every corpse between here and the stairs, because they have. They're wearing three people's armour and none of it fits.

They loot everything. Bodies, chests, camps, you. They'll take your kills, your drops and your pants if you leave them on a radiator. They're the reason every loot box on the floor is already open when you get there.
The thing is, they're not bad people. They're people who worked out early that the dungeon doesn't care, and decided not to either. They'd rob your corpse, sure. But they'd close its eyes first.

Strengths: they're ruthless, they're organised and they've got everything you were about to find. Weaknesses: they bicker constantly, they don't trust each other, and they'll bail the second a fight goes wrong.
Shake them down, pay them off, or run with them a while. One day, one of the twins will save your life, and she'll never let you forget it.
